        ### Question
        A previously healthy 48-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of a nonpruritic rash on his right forearm. The rash began as pustules and progressed to form nodules and ulcers. He works as a gardener. Physical examination shows right axillary lymphadenopathy and the findings in the photograph. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

        ### Options
        opa. Pasteurella multocida
opb. Pseudomonas aeruginosa
opc. Bartonella henselae
opd. Blastomyces dermatitidis
ope. Sporothrix schenckii

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Exposure to soil and plants as a gardener -> Inoculation of the skin -> Development of nodules and ulcers -> 70% CHAIN: Right axillary lymphadenopathy present -> Suggestive of an infectious etiology -> Consideration of an organism causing skin lesions and lymphadenopathy -> 80% CHAIN: Nonpruritic rash on the right forearm with pustules progressing to nodules and ulcers -> Suggestive of an infectious process -> 75% CHAIN: Gardener profession -> Increased risk of exposure to environmental pathogens -> Consideration of fungal or bacterial organisms -> 70% CHAIN: Clinical presentation with nodules and ulcers -> Suggestive of a granulomatous response -> Possible involvement of an intracellular organism -> 60% CHAIN: Considering the clinical presentation and occupational exposure -> Bartonella henselae, the causative agent of cat scratch disease, is the most likely organism -> 70%
